text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right to Education as a Fundamental Right?
textHi: भारतीय संविधान का कौन सा अनुच्छेद शिक्षा के अधिकार को मौलिक अधिकार के रूप में प्रदान करता है?

options.whyIncorrect: Article 19 covers freedoms of speech, assembly, movement, etc.
Article 45 (DPSP) now covers early childhood care and education for children below 6.
Article 32 is the right to constitutional remedies.

explanation: Article 21-A, inserted by the 86th Amendment (2002), mandates free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14. Implemented through the RTE Act 2009 from 1 April 2010.

text: The Indian Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
textHi: भारतीय संविधान को संविधान सभा द्वारा कब अंगीकृत किया गया?

options.whyIncorrect: That is Independence Day.
That is when the Constitution came into force (Republic Day).
That was the first sitting of the Constituent Assembly.

explanation: Adopted 26 Nov 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day/Samvidhan Divas since 2015); came into force 26 Jan 1950. Drafting Committee chairman: Dr B.R. Ambedkar; President of Constituent Assembly: Dr Rajendra Prasad; took 2 years 11 months 18 days.
source: Constitution of India — historical background (NCERT Class 9 Political Science)

text: The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn by Gandhiji in 1922 after which incident?
textHi: 1922 में गांधीजी ने किस घटना के बाद असहयोग आंदोलन वापस ले लिया?

options.whyIncorrect: Jallianwala Bagh (1919) preceded and partly triggered the movement.
Kakori (1925) was a revolutionary action by HRA, after the movement ended.
Simon Commission came in 1928.

explanation: At Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur, UP) on 4 Feb 1922, a mob burnt a police station killing 22 policemen. Gandhiji, committed to non-violence, called off the movement (Bardoli resolution, 12 Feb 1922). Note the UP connection — important for the 'प्रदेश' angle.
source: NCERT Class 10 History, Nationalism in India
examRelevance: Freedom struggle events with UP links are high-yield.

text: Who founded the Arya Samaj in 1875?
textHi: 1875 में आर्य समाज की स्थापना किसने की?

options.whyIncorrect: He founded the Brahmo Samaj (1828).
He founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897).
He founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873).

explanation: Dayanand Saraswati founded Arya Samaj in Bombay (1875) with the slogan 'Back to the Vedas'; wrote Satyarth Prakash; DAV schools carry his legacy. Reformer–organisation pairs are very commonly asked.
source: NCERT Class 8 History, Women, Caste and Reform

text: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?
textHi: किस ग्रह को 'लाल ग्रह' कहा जाता है?

options.whyIncorrect: Venus is the 'Morning/Evening Star' and Earth's twin.
Jupiter is the largest planet.
Saturn is known for its rings.

explanation: Mars appears red due to iron oxide on its surface. India's Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission, 2013–14) made ISRO the first Asian agency to reach Mars orbit. Order of planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
source: NCERT Class 6 Geography, The Earth in the Solar System

text: The Indian Standard Time (IST) is based on the longitude:
textHi: भारतीय मानक समय (IST) किस देशांतर पर आधारित है?

options.whyIncorrect: 0° is the Prime Meridian — GMT/UTC reference.
That is India's westernmost longitude (Gujarat).
That is India's easternmost longitude (Arunachal Pradesh).

explanation: IST = UTC + 5:30, based on 82°30' E which passes near Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh. India's longitudinal extent (68°7'–97°25' E) means ~2 hours of solar-time difference between Gujarat and Arunachal.
source: NCERT Class 9 Geography, India — Size and Location

text: Which is the longest river of Uttar Pradesh by length within the state?
textHi: उत्तर प्रदेश में राज्य के भीतर लंबाई के अनुसार सबसे लंबी नदी कौन सी है?

options.whyIncorrect: Yamuna is long but the Ganga's course within UP is longer.
Gomti (Lucknow) is entirely within UP but much shorter (~900 km).
Ghaghara is a major tributary but shorter within UP.

explanation: The Ganga flows about 1,000+ km through UP (from Bijnor to Ballia) — the longest course within the state. Key UP rivers: Ganga, Yamuna, Ghaghara, Gomti, Ramganga, Betwa, Ken, Son, Sharda, Rapti.
examRelevance: Rivers of UP — likely under 'प्रदेश' angle.

text: Who is the constitutional head of a State in India?
textHi: भारत में किसी राज्य का संवैधानिक प्रमुख कौन होता है?

options.whyIncorrect: The CM is the real executive head, not the constitutional head.
The Speaker presides over the Assembly.
Heads the state judiciary.

explanation: Article 153–154: the Governor is the constitutional (nominal) head of the state, appointed by the President for 5 years; the Council of Ministers headed by the CM exercises real executive power (Art. 163).
source: NCERT Class 9–10 Political Science; Constitution Part VI
examRelevance: 'Our governance system' — Governor/CM roles frequently asked.

text: A triangular road sign with a red border generally indicates:
textHi: लाल किनारे वाला त्रिभुजाकार सड़क चिह्न सामान्यतः क्या दर्शाता है?

options.whyIncorrect: Mandatory/regulatory signs are circular.

options.text: A warning/caution (e.g., school ahead, sharp bend)

options.whyIncorrect: Informatory signs are rectangular, usually blue.
Parking signs are informatory rectangles.

explanation: Indian road signs: Mandatory — circular (red border prohibitory, blue compulsory); Cautionary/Warning — triangular with red border; Informatory — rectangular. Road Safety Week is observed in January; Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act 2019 raised penalties.
source: Indian Roads Congress road-sign classification; MoRTH
examRelevance: Traffic and road safety is an explicit syllabus topic.

text: The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) is headed by:
textHi: राष्ट्रीय आपदा प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण (NDMA) का अध्यक्ष कौन होता है?

options.whyIncorrect: The President is not part of NDMA.
Disaster management falls under MHA, but the PM chairs NDMA.
Armed forces assist but do not head NDMA.

explanation: NDMA was constituted under the Disaster Management Act 2005 with the PM as Chairperson; State DMAs are chaired by CMs and District DMAs by District Collectors/Magistrates. NDRF is the specialised response force. 13 October: International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction.
examRelevance: Disaster management institutional structure — frequent question.

text: The innermost layer of the Earth is called the:
textHi: पृथ्वी की सबसे भीतरी परत कहलाती है:

options.whyIncorrect: The crust is the outermost, thinnest layer.
The mantle lies between crust and core.
Lithosphere = crust + upper mantle (rigid outer shell).

explanation: Layers: Crust (SiAl), Mantle (SiMa), Core (NiFe — nickel and iron; outer core liquid, inner core solid). Core radius ≈ 3,500 km; temperature up to ~5,000–6,000 °C.
source: NCERT Class 7 Geography, Inside Our Earth
examRelevance: Structure of the Earth — first topic in the EVS syllabus list.

text: Which of the following is a direct tax in India?
textHi: निम्न में से कौन भारत में प्रत्यक्ष कर है?

options.whyIncorrect: GST is an indirect tax on consumption.
Customs duty on imports is indirect.
Excise (on petroleum, alcohol etc.) is indirect.

explanation: Direct taxes are paid by the person on whom they are levied (income tax, corporate tax); indirect taxes are shifted to consumers (GST, customs, excise). GST introduced 1 July 2017 via the 101st Constitutional Amendment.
source: NCERT Class 10 Economics; Ministry of Finance

text: Which classical dance form originated in Uttar Pradesh?
textHi: कौन सा शास्त्रीय नृत्य उत्तर प्रदेश से उत्पन्न हुआ?

options.whyIncorrect: Tamil Nadu.
Odisha.
Andhra Pradesh.

explanation: Kathak (from 'katha' — story) developed in North India with major gharanas at Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras. Birju Maharaj (Lucknow gharana) was its most celebrated exponent. The 8 Sangeet Natak Akademi classical dances: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Sattriya.
source: Sangeet Natak Akademi; NCERT Class 11 Fine Arts
examRelevance: Cultural heritage with UP link — high probability.

options.text: Protection of forests by hugging trees, led by villagers in Uttarakhand (then UP)
Protest against big dams on the Narmada
options.whyIncorrect: That is the Narmada Bachao Andolan (Medha Patkar).
Unrelated.
Unrelated.

explanation: Chipko began in Chamoli district (then in Uttar Pradesh, now Uttarakhand), with Sunderlal Bahuguna, Chandi Prasad Bhatt and Gaura Devi. It inspired the Forest Conservation Act 1980. Similar: Appiko movement (Karnataka, 1983).
source: NCERT Class 10 Science, Management of Natural Resources
